literal: Zu Xi bore a grudge and thereupon informed Yuan Kang's two younger brothers, Shu Chen and Ji Ji, and the others.
idiomatic: Zu Xi nursed a grudge and told Yuan Kang's younger brothers Shu Chen and Ji Ji, among others.

literal: Shu Chen told Yang Yin; Yin frowned and answered, "I fear it will not benefit the dead."
idiomatic: Shu Chen told Yang Yin. Yin knit his brow and said, "I doubt that will help the dead."

literal: Because of this it was halted.
idiomatic: On that account the matter was dropped.

literal: When Wenxuan was regent, Ting proposed to fill more than ten clerk posts; all had taken bribes; by law they should be strangled, but the sovereign eventually pardoned them.
idiomatic: When Wenxuan was regent, Ting proposed more than ten clerk appointments, every one of them bought. By law they merited strangulation, but in the end the sovereign let them off.

literal: He also stole one copy of the official Comprehensive Digest from the office.
idiomatic: He also stole an office copy of the Comprehensive Digest.

literal: When it came to light, Wenxuan entrusted Attendant of the Masters of Writing Wang Tuya to investigate, and also wrote to Prince of Pingyang Yan, ordering him to take Ting into custody and not allow escape.
idiomatic: When the theft came to light, Wenxuan put Attendant of the Masters of Writing Wang Tuya in charge of the inquiry and wrote Prince of Pingyang Yan as well, telling him to take Ting into custody and allow no escape.

literal: Yan sent Field Officer Sun Zikuan to summon him; Ting accepted the summons, then at once fled in secret.
idiomatic: Yan sent field officer Sun Zikuan to fetch him. Ting answered the summons, then slipped away the same night.

literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Gao Dezheng was deputy for matters at the secondary capital; they plotted, saying, "Ting knows his guilt—panic flight is only natural, but proclaim an order to the Secretariat, saying, 'By Bingzhou constraint, distribute three sets of the Five Classics; the Deputy Director is to inspect and expedite in person'—thus Ting will feel secure and return home at night; then seize him."
idiomatic: Yellow gate gentleman Gao Dezheng was deputy for affairs at the secondary capital. They plotted: "Ting knows he is guilty and will bolt—that is only natural. But issue an order to the secretariat, saying, 'By Bingzhou's command, distribute three sets of the Five Classics; the deputy director is to inspect and hurry delivery in person.' Then Ting will feel safe, come home at night, and we can take him."

literal: Ting did indeed follow Dezheng's plan and returned home.
idiomatic: Ting did exactly as Dezheng had planned and went home.

literal: Toward evening they raided his house, bound Ting, and sent him to the Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: Near dusk they raided his house, bound him, and sent him to the minister of justice.

literal: According to the crimes, illegal conduct warranted strangulation.
idiomatic: By the charges, his illegal acts called for strangulation.

literal: Wenxuan, because Ting had served previous generations, hinted to the office to specially mitigate the punishment; a memorial was submitted to spare death and remove his name from the register.
idiomatic: Wenxuan, because Ting had served the house in earlier reigns, hinted that the office should show special leniency. The memorial asked to spare his life and strike his name from the rolls.

literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was again summoned to follow the imperial carriage; by precedent for removal from office he participated at Jinyang.
idiomatic: In Tianbao's first year he was summoned again to follow the carriage. Under the usual rule for men struck from office, he took part at Jinyang.

literal: Ting was naturally clever; nothing was hard for him to learn; of every craft and skill none did he neglect to take up; beyond literature he was skilled at music, understood the languages of the four barbarians and yin-yang divination, and medicine above all was his forte.
idiomatic: Ting was clever by nature; nothing was hard for him to learn. Of every craft and art he took hold; beyond letters he knew music, the tongues of the four quarters, and yin-yang divination—and medicine above all was what he did best.

literal: Emperor Wenxuan, though he disliked Ting's repeated violations of law, loved his talents and skills and ordered him to serve directly in the Secretariat, drafting edicts.
idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan disliked how often Ting broke the law, yet loved his talents and kept him in the secretariat drafting edicts.

literal: Ting sent a secret report denouncing Secretariat Attendant Lu Yuangui; an edict ordered Pei Ying to interrogate him; Yuangui, in answering, offended the intent and was assigned to the works compound.
idiomatic: Ting sent a secret denunciation of secretariat attendant Lu Yuangui. An edict ordered Pei Ying to question him. Yuangui's answers offended the throne and he was sent to the works compound.

literal: Ting was appointed Superintendent of Medicines; soon he was promoted to Imperial Pharmacy Director.
idiomatic: Ting was made superintendent of medicines and soon promoted to director of the imperial pharmacy.

literal: He also memorialized to make walnut oil and again was removed from office for embezzling from the storehouses.
idiomatic: He also memorialized to supply walnut oil and again lost his post for skimming the storehouses.

literal: Whenever Wenxuan saw him he always called him "thief."
idiomatic: Whenever Wenxuan saw him he called him "thief."

literal: When Wenxuan died, in the general selection of meritorious veterans he was made Administrator of Ningwu.
idiomatic: When Wenxuan died, in the general selection of old servants he was made administrator of Ningwu.

literal: It happened that Yang Yin and the others were executed; he did not take up the post and was appointed Compiler in the Writings Office.
idiomatic: Yang Yin and the others were executed just then; he never took up the post and was made a compiler in the writings office.

literal: He repeatedly sent secret memorials and incurred Emperor Xiaozhao's resentment; an edict ordered the Secretariat and the Masters of Writing to cut off Ting's access to memorials.
idiomatic: He sent secret memorials again and again until Emperor Xiaozhao grew furious. An edict barred the secretariat and masters of writing from accepting his papers.

literal: Ting was skilled at making walnut oil for painting and presented it to the Prince of Changgang, saying, "Your Highness has extraordinary bone structure; Xiao Zheng dreamed that Your Highness rode a dragon into heaven."
idiomatic: Ting knew how to make walnut oil for painting and offered it to the Prince of Changgang, saying, "Your Highness has the bones of an uncommon man. Xiao Zheng dreamed you rode a dragon into heaven."

literal: The prince said to him, "If that is so, then my elder brother ought to grow very rich."
idiomatic: The prince said, "If that is so, my elder brother should grow very rich indeed."

literal: When he took the throne he was Emperor Wucheng and promoted Ting to Secretariat Attendant.
idiomatic: When he took the throne as Emperor Wucheng, he promoted Ting to secretariat attendant.

literal: The emperor had Ting play the pipa in the rear garden while He Shikai performed Hu dance; each was rewarded with a hundred bolts of goods.
idiomatic: In the rear garden the emperor had Ting play the pipa while He Shikai danced the Hu step. Each man received a hundred bolts of goods.

literal: Shikai envied him and had him sent out as Administrator of Ande, then transferred to Administrator of Qi commandery; because his mother was old he begged to return and serve her, and an edict permitted it.
idiomatic: Shikai envied him and sent him out as administrator of Ande, then moved him to Qi commandery. His mother was old; he begged to return and tend her, and the edict allowed it.

literal: It happened that envoys from the south came on a mission of courtesy; he was made commissioner for receiving guests.
idiomatic: When envoys came from the south on a courtesy mission, he was made commissioner for receiving them.

literal: Soon he was Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Acting Three Excellencies of Honor, drafting edicts.
idiomatic: Soon he was vice director of the imperial ancestral temple, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and acting three excellencies of honor, drafting edicts.

literal: At first, during the Qianming and Huangjian eras, Ting knew that Wucheng harbored great designs in secret and therefore bonded with him deeply, currying favor with obsequious devotion.
idiomatic: Early in the Qianming and Huangjian reigns Ting saw that Wucheng nursed great designs in secret and bound himself to him, flattering him at every turn.

literal: Wucheng in the Tianbao era had often been blamed and always harbored resentment in his heart.
idiomatic: In the Tianbao years Wucheng had been blamed again and again and carried the grudge in his heart.

literal: Ting now toed the emperor's wishes memorialized to posthumously honor Grand Ancestor as Emperor Shenwu and change High Ancestor Emperor Wenxuan's title to Weizong Jinglie Emperor, to please Wucheng; the emperor assented.
idiomatic: Ting now played to the throne and memorialized to posthumously honor Gao Huan as Emperor Shenwu and change High Ancestor Wenxuan's temple style to Weizong Jinglie Emperor. Wucheng was pleased and assented.

literal: At the time the empress loved her younger son, Prince Dongping Yan, and wished to make him heir; Wucheng, because the Later Sovereign by proper succession was eldest, found it hard to shift the succession.
idiomatic: The empress then doted on her younger son, Prince Dongping Yan, and wanted him for heir. Wucheng, because the Later Sovereign stood first in proper order, found the succession hard to move.

literal: Ting said privately to Shikai, "Your favor is unmatched in all antiquity; when the imperial carriage one day halts at evening, how will you see it through to the end?"
idiomatic: Ting said privately to He Shikai, "Your favor has no match in all antiquity. When the carriage halts one evening, how will you finish your days?"

literal: Shikai thereupon asked him for a stratagem.
idiomatic: Shikai thereupon asked him for a plan.

literal: Ting said, "You should persuade the sovereign, saying that the sons of Emperor Xiang, Emperor Xuan, and Emperor Zhao all could not be enthroned; now the crown prince should early tread the great position to fix the relation of ruler and minister.
idiomatic: Ting said, "Persuade the sovereign that the sons of Emperor Xiang, Emperor Xuan, and Emperor Zhao could none of them take the throne. Now the crown prince should ascend early and fix ruler and minister in their places.

literal: If the affair succeeds, the empress and the young sovereign will both owe you virtue—this is a plan of ten thousand certainties.
idiomatic: If it succeeds, empress and young sovereign alike will owe you their fortune—a plan without a crack in it.

literal: You for now hint a little, let the sovereign roughly understand; Ting will from outside submit a memorial arguing it."
idiomatic: You hint a little for now until he roughly understands. I will argue it from outside in a memorial."

literal: Shikai promised.
idiomatic: He Shikai agreed.

literal: Thereupon a comet appeared; the Grand Astrologer memorialized that it was an omen for removing the old and spreading the new.
idiomatic: Then a comet appeared. The grand astrologer reported it as an omen to remove the old and spread the new.

literal: Ting thereupon submitted a memorial, saying, "Though Your Majesty is Son of Heaven, you are not yet supremely exalted.
idiomatic: Ting then memorialized: "Though Your Majesty is Son of Heaven, you are not yet at the summit of honor.

literal: According to the Spring and Autumn Yuanming Bao it says: 'In the year yiyou, remove the old and reform the government.'
idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Yuanming Bao says, 'In the yiyou year, remove the old and reform the government.'

literal: This year the Grand Year is yiyou; the Eastern Palace should receive the succession, that the distinction of ruler and minister be early fixed, and also to answer above to the Way of Heaven."
idiomatic: This year's Grand Year is yiyou. The Eastern Palace should receive the succession so ruler and minister are fixed early—and so answer Heaven above."

literal: He also submitted the precedent of Wei Emperor Xianwen's abdication to his son.
idiomatic: He also cited Wei Emperor Xianwen's abdication to his son.

literal: The emperor followed it.
idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

literal: Thereupon he was made Director of the Secretariat and Acting Three Excellencies of Honor, and received great personal favor.
idiomatic: He was made director of the secretariat and acting three excellencies of honor and grew greatly in favor.

literal: Once he was valued by both palaces, he set his heart on the chancellorship.
idiomatic: Once both palaces valued him, he set his heart on the chancellorship.

literal: He had earlier been friendly with Secretariat Attendant Liu Ti; he therefore memorialized the crimes of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing Zhao Yanshen, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director Yuan Wenyao, and Attendant-in-Ordinary He Shikai, ordering Ti to present the memorial.
idiomatic: He had been friendly with secretariat attendant Liu Ti. He now memorialized the crimes of attendant-in-ordinary and director of the masters of writing Zhao Yanshen, attendant-in-ordinary and left vice director Yuan Wenyao, and attendant-in-ordinary He Shikai, and told Ti to present it.

literal: Ti feared and did not dare pass it through; the affair leaked somewhat; Yanshen and the others first went to the emperor and confessed themselves.
idiomatic: Ti was afraid and did not dare forward it. Word leaked. Yanshen and the others went first to the emperor and confessed.

literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, seized Ting, and interrogated him, saying, "Why do you ruin my Shikai?"
idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, seized Ting, and demanded, "Why do you ruin my Shikai?"

literal: Ting thereupon said in a harsh voice, "Your servant advanced through Shikai and originally had no wish to ruin him; since Your Majesty now questions your servant, your servant dares not answer except with the truth.
idiomatic: Ting answered in a harsh voice, "I rose through Shikai and never meant to ruin him. Since Your Majesty asks, I dare not answer except with the truth.

literal: Shikai, Wenyao, Yanshen, and the others monopolize authority, control the court, and with Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wei Jin communicate inside and outside as outer and inner; they sell offices and peddle judgments; government is bought with bribes—the songs of the realm say it.
idiomatic: Shikai, Wenyao, Yanshen, and the rest twist power and run the court. With director of the ministry of personnel Wei Jin they traffic inside and out, outer shell and inner hand, selling offices and peddling verdicts until government is bought with bribes—the realm sings of it.

literal: If men with understanding knew this, how could it be heard in the four quarters!
idiomatic: If men with eyes knew this, how could it reach the four quarters and stand?

literal: Your Majesty takes no heed; your servant fears the great enterprise of Qi will be ruined."
idiomatic: Your Majesty pays no heed. I fear the great enterprise of Qi is being ruined."

literal: The emperor said, "You are slandering me!"
idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are slandering me!"

literal: Ting said, "Your servant does not dare slander; Your Majesty took a man's daughter."
idiomatic: Ting said, "I do not slander. Your Majesty took a man's daughter."

literal: The emperor said, "I took her because she was poor and hungry, and therefore adopted her."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "I took her because she was poor and starving and I adopted her."

literal: Ting said, "Why not open the granaries and give relief, yet buy her and bring her into the rear palace?"
idiomatic: Ting said, "Why not open the granaries and give relief, instead of buying her into the rear palace?"

literal: The emperor grew still angrier, struck his mouth with the knife ring, and canes and clubs fell in disorder; he was about to beat him to death.
idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier still, struck his mouth with the knife ring, and blows from cane and club rained down until they were ready to beat him dead.

literal: He shouted, "If you do not kill your servant, Your Majesty gains a name; if you kill your servant, your servant gains a name.
idiomatic: He shouted, "If you do not kill me, Your Majesty wins a name. Kill me, and I win a name.

literal: If you wish for a name, do not kill your servant; your servant will compound golden elixir for Your Majesty."
idiomatic: If you want a name, do not kill me—I will compound golden elixir for Your Majesty."

literal: Thereupon he was slightly granted reprieve.
idiomatic: On that he was spared, a little.

literal: Ting also said, "Your Majesty has one Fan Zeng you cannot use—what is to be known from that?"
idiomatic: Ting also said, "Your Majesty has a Fan Zeng you will not use—what does that tell you?"

literal: The emperor was angry again and said, "You make yourself Fan Zeng and take me for Xiang Yu!"
idiomatic: The emperor raged again. "You make yourself Fan Zeng and call me Xiang Yu!"

literal: Ting said, "Xiang Yu as a man—how could he be reached? Only Heaven's mandate did not arrive.
idiomatic: Ting said, "Xiang Yu as a man—who could match him? Only Heaven's mandate never came.

literal: Xiang Yu in plain cloth led a rabble host and in five years achieved the hegemon's enterprise.
idiomatic: Xiang Yu in plain cloth led a rabble army and in five years built a hegemon's realm.

literal: Your Majesty by your father's and elder brother's resources attained only to this; your servant holds that Xiang Yu is not lightly to be despised.
idiomatic: Your Majesty, on your father's and brother's capital, reached only this. I say Xiang Yu is not to be despised lightly.

literal: Your servant is not merely to be compared with Fan Zeng—even Zhang Liang cannot be reached.
idiomatic: I am not merely Fan Zeng's equal—even Zhang Liang falls short of me.

literal: Zhang Liang personally attended the heir apparent, yet still relied on the Four Whiteheads of Shang Mountain to fix Han's succession.
idiomatic: Zhang Liang attended the heir in person, yet still needed the Four Whiteheads of Shang Mountain to settle Han's succession.

literal: Your servant's post is not that of chief minister; I am an outsider, yet exhaust loyalty and urge Your Majesty to abdicate, making Your Majesty honored as Grand Emperor and your son seated at the imperial hinge—for yourself and your son alike, preserving blessed fortune.
idiomatic: I am no chief minister, only an outsider, yet I spend myself in loyalty, urging Your Majesty to abdicate so you stand honored as grand emperor and your son holds the hinge—for you and your son alike, fortune preserved.

literal: That petty Zhang Liang—how is he worth counting!
idiomatic: That scrap of a Zhang Liang—what is he worth counting!"

literal: The emperor grew still more furious and ordered earth stuffed into his mouth; Ting spat and spoke, never bending.
idiomatic: The emperor grew still more furious and ordered earth stuffed into his mouth. Ting spat and spoke on, never bending.

literal: He was then flogged two hundred strokes and assigned to the works compound; soon he was transferred to Guang province.
idiomatic: They flogged him two hundred strokes and sent him to the works compound; soon he was moved to Guang province.

literal: Inspector Li Zuxun treated him very generously.
idiomatic: Inspector Li Zuxun treated him very generously.

literal: Vice Director Zhang Fengli, to please the great ministers, memorialized, "Though Ting is a banished convict, he constantly sits facing the inspector as an equal."
idiomatic: Vice director Zhang Fengli, courting the great ministers, memorialized, "Though Ting is a banished man, he constantly sits facing the inspector as an equal."

literal: An edict replied, "Imprison him in a cell."
idiomatic: The edict answered, "Put him in a cell."

literal: Fengli said, "'Cell' means an underground pit."
idiomatic: Fengli said, "'Cell' means a pit in the earth."

literal: A deep pit was therefore dug and he was placed within; harsh restrictions were added; fetters never left his body; family and kin were not permitted to visit.
idiomatic: They dug a deep pit and put him in it, tightened every guard, and fetters never left his body. Kin were forbidden to visit.

literal: In the night they used turnip-seed candles to smoke his eyes; because of this he went blind.
idiomatic: At night they burned turnip-seed candles to smoke his eyes, and he went blind.

literal: When Wucheng died, the Later Sovereign remembered him and at once appointed him Inspector of Hai province.
idiomatic: When Wucheng died, the Later Sovereign remembered him and at once made him inspector of Hai province.

literal: At the time Lu Lingxuan meddled in court affairs from outside; her son Mu Tipo was a favorite.
idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan then meddled in court affairs from outside, and her son Mu Tipo stood in favor.

literal: Ting therefore sent a letter to Dame Lu's younger brother Sida, saying, "Zhao Yanshen's heart is deep and hidden; he wishes to perform the Yi and Huo deed—the Lady's brother and sister, how can they be secure? Why not early employ a man of counsel?"
idiomatic: Ting sent a letter to Dame Lu's younger brother Sida: "Zhao Yanshen's heart runs deep and hidden. He means to play Yi Yin and Huo Guang—the lady's brother and sister, how will they stay safe? Why not take a clever man into counsel early?"

literal: He Shikai also, because Ting could decide great affairs, wished to make him chief strategist; therefore he set aside old enmity and waited on him with an open heart.
idiomatic: He Shikai too, because Ting could decide great affairs, wanted him for chief strategist, set aside old grudges, and received him with an open heart.

literal: Together with Dame Lu he spoke to the emperor, saying, "Of the three emperors Xiang, Xuan, and Zhao, none of their sons could be enthroned; that the Present Sovereign still holds the imperial position is truly because of Ancestor Xiao Zheng.
idiomatic: With Dame Lu he told the emperor, "Of Emperors Xiang, Xuan, and Zhao, not one son could take the throne. That the Present Sovereign still sits there is truly Ancestor Xiao Zheng's doing.

literal: This man has great merit and ought to be repaid with heavy grace.
idiomatic: The man has great merit and should be repaid in full.

literal: Though Xiao Zheng's heart and conduct are thin, his strange stratagems surpass other men; in urgency he may truly be relied upon.
idiomatic: Xiao Zheng's heart is thin, but his stratagems surpass other men; in urgency he may truly be trusted.

literal: Moreover he is blind in both eyes and surely has no thought of rebellion; please summon him and ask his plans."
idiomatic: And he is blind in both eyes—surely he has no thought of rebellion. Summon him and ask his counsel."

literal: The emperor followed this; he entered office as Silver-Green Grand Master of the Palace, Director of the Secretariat, and Acting Grand Three Excellencies of Honor.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed. Ting entered as silver-green grand master of the palace, director of the secretariat, and acting grand three excellencies of honor.

literal: After He Shikai died, he again persuaded Dame Lu to remove Yanshen and made Ting Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: After He Shikai died he again urged Dame Lu to remove Yanshen and made Ting attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: At Jinyang he sent a secret memorial asking to execute the Prince of Langya.
idiomatic: At Jinyang he sent a secret memorial asking to execute the Prince of Langya.

literal: Once the plan was carried out, he was gradually entrusted with greater favor.
idiomatic: Once the plan succeeded, favor on him grew step by step.

literal: Also, when the empress dowager was confined, Ting wished to make Dame Lu empress dowager; he compiled the Wei precedents for emperor's mother and empress dowager and spoke of them to the Grand Dame.
idiomatic: When the empress dowager was confined, Ting wished to make Dame Lu empress dowager. He compiled Wei precedents on the emperor's mother and empress dowager and laid them before the Grand Dame.

literal: He said to others, "Though the Grand Dame is called a woman, in truth she is a hero; since Nüwa there has been none like her."
idiomatic: He told others, "Though the Grand Dame is called a woman, she is a hero in truth—since Nüwa there has been no one like her."

literal: The Grand Dame also called Ting State Teacher and National Treasure.
idiomatic: The Grand Dame in turn called Ting State Teacher and National Treasure.

literal: Thereupon he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, supervised the National History, specially advanced, entered the Forest of Literature, oversaw compilation, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan commandery, drew salary from Taiyuan commandery dry grain, and was given seventy soldiers.
idiomatic: He was made left vice director of the masters of writing, supervised the national history, given special advancement, entered the Forest of Literature to oversee compilation, enfeoffed as duke of Yan commandery, drew dry grain from Taiyuan commandery, and was given seventy soldiers.

literal: His residence was in Yijing Ward; he expanded neighboring houses and undertook great construction; Dame Lu herself went to inspect the work on site.
idiomatic: His house stood in Yijing Ward. He bought out neighbors and undertook great building; Dame Lu herself went to inspect the work.

literal: His power bent the court and field.
idiomatic: His power bent court and countryside.

literal: Hulü Guang deeply hated him; seeing him from afar he would secretly curse, saying, "Busy beggarly little man—what schemes does he mean to run!"
idiomatic: Hulü Guang hated him deeply. Seeing him from afar he would mutter, "Busy beggarly little man—what scheme is he running now!"

literal: He often told the generals, "Border news and disposition of troops—Director Zhao often discussed them with us.
idiomatic: He often told the generals, "Border news and the disposition of troops—Director Zhao used to debate them with us.

literal: A blind man holds the secrets and will not speak with us at all—I only fear he will ruin the state's affairs."
idiomatic: A blind man holds the secrets and will not speak with us at all. I only fear he will ruin the state's affairs."
